title: The Fox and the Stork
text:
A fox and a stork were on friendly terms, and one day the fox invited the stork to dinner. As a joke, he served the meal as a thin soup poured into a wide, shallow dish. The fox lapped it up easily. The stork, with her long narrow beak, could only wet the tip of it and went home as hungry as she had come. The fox said he was sorry she had not enjoyed the soup.

The stork did not complain. A few days later she invited the fox to dine with her in return. When he arrived, hungry and pleased with himself, a delicious smell of food filled the air. But the stork served it in a tall jar with a long, narrow neck.

The stork put her beak into the jar and ate comfortably. The fox could only lick the outside of the jar and sniff at the rim. He had to go home with an empty stomach. He could not even protest, because he knew exactly where the idea had come from.
lesson: The way you treat people is the way you teach them to treat you. A cheap trick played on someone usually comes back to you in the same form.
source: Aesop's Fables (Perry Index 426); La Fontaine, Fables I.18
